Reading vs. Seeing

When we see something, we generally take it in all at once.

However, when we read, we typically read in a sequence, one word at a time. We could say that reading has a dimension of  .

When we're looking at images, it doesn't really matter what image we saw previously.

However, as we read across time (t), what we've seen previously matters a LOT! It provides   to the token we're currently seeing.

Weakness of RNNs

If I want to measure how "cat" should affect "and", I have to go back through 5 "context blocks" (h2 to h6). Since these are "compressions" we lose a lot of meaning/context from things earlier in the sequence. RNNs struggle with " ".

Producing output from a transformer

With our context-aware embeddings, we can then pass those into a simple feed-forward neural network to produce an output prediction (similar to producing an output with an RNN). If we only wanted to predict the next word, we only need the   context-aware embedding (output is size 9 because we have 9 words in our vocab).

Training a Transformer

Self-Attention · Training22

Transformers and the Brain

Schrimpf et al. (PNAS, 2021) compared 43 language models against people's brain activity (fMRI and electrodes) on the same sentences.

  • Transformers matched best, predicting nearly 100% of the explainable variance in the brain's responses.
  • How well a model matched the brain tracked how good it was at  , not at other language tasks.

Careful: this is a match in what gets predicted, not evidence that neurons compute softmax(Q KT / √dk) V.

Self-Attention · Programming Day26

Self Attention Analogy

Another mental model for self-attention might be "using tinder", where everyone on the app is simultaneously looking for someone and being looked at.

  • Q – Query: What each person is looking for in a person
    • "I'm looking for a 10/10 terrachad ASU frat leader"
  • K – Key: the first photo each person has on their profile
    • "I'm a rocket"
  • V – Value: The rest of the profile
Self-Attention · Programming Day27

Self Attention Analogy

  • Q – Query: What each person is looking for in a person
    • "I'm looking for a 10/10 terrachad ASU frat leader"
  • K – Key: the first photo each person has on their profile
    • "I'm a baddie"
  • V – Value: The rest of the profile

As you swipe through profiles, you glance at the key of everyone (their first photo) and calculate how much they match your query (ASU frat leader) while everyone else is also doing the same.

Based on this, you calculate how much attention you should pay to all the values (actual profiles) of people you see.
